Liner, flute, liner: the structure behind every Avyaan box.

How our automatic 3 ply line works.

A 3 ply plant turns rolls of kraft paper into finished corrugated sheets and cartons in one continuous, machine-controlled process.

Paper reels are loaded

Three paper reels feed the line: an outer liner, an inner liner and a fluting medium for the centre.

The flute is formed

Heated rollers shape the fluting paper into its wave pattern, the layer that gives corrugated board its cushioning and stacking strength.

Layers are glued together

Starch adhesive bonds the fluted layer to the liners under controlled heat and pressure, forming a flat 3 ply sheet.

Sheets are cut and creased

The board is trimmed to size and creased so that boxes fold cleanly and keep their shape.

Boxes are finished

Sheets are slotted, die-cut, pasted or stitched into final cartons, ready for dispatch.

Uniform strength

Machine-controlled glue and pressure give an even bond across the whole sheet.

Accurate sizes

Automatic cutting and creasing keeps every box the same size, so packing lines run smoothly.

Less wastage

Precise trimming and fewer rejects mean better use of material and fairer pricing.

Faster output

Continuous production lets us handle bulk and repeat orders without slowing down.

What corrugated board is made of.

Three layers of paper do all the work, held together by adhesive.

Liner paper

The flat outer and inner sheets. They give the box its printable surface and resist puncture and tearing.

Fluting medium

The wavy middle paper. Its shape creates air channels that cushion impact and carry load.

Adhesive

Starch-based glue bonds the flute to both liners. A good, even bond is what keeps the layers from peeling apart.

Paper quality

Paper weight (GSM) and bursting factor (BF) set how strong the final board can be.

Print tips for corrugated boxes.

Mind the folds

Keep important text and logos away from folds, flap edges and seams so they stay readable.

Use strong contrast

Dark ink on kraft board reads best. Colours look slightly muted on brown board compared to white paper.

Leave space for labels

Keep a clear area for barcodes, dispatch labels and batch stickers.

Add handling marks

Marks such as Fragile, This Side Up and Keep Dry protect your goods all along the supply chain.

Common corrugated box styles.

Tell us your product and we will suggest the style that fits.

Regular slotted carton

The standard shipping box. Flaps fold in and meet at the middle. Simple, strong and economical.

Die-cut box

Cut and creased to a custom shape. Folds into form, often without glue, for neat retail and display packs.

Telescopic box

A two-piece cap and base. Good for heavy or tall items such as appliances and furniture parts.

Tray and flap tray

Open or low-sided trays for sweets, food items and displays.

Mailer box

Self-locking box for e-commerce and courier shipments.

Layer pads and partitions

Separate items inside a carton to stop rubbing and breakage.

Corrugated boxes: what you should know.

Corrugated board is made of paper layers. In a 3 ply box, a fluted (wavy) sheet is sandwiched between two flat liners. The air pockets inside the flutes absorb impact and carry stacking loads, which is why a light box can protect a heavy product.

A flute, made at Avyaan

Maximum cushioning

Thicker flute with good cushioning and stacking strength. Suited to fragile and heavier items.

B flute

Strong and printable

Thinner flute with a flatter surface and good crush resistance. Suited to printed cartons and packaged goods.

C flute

All-round choice

A balance of cushioning and strength. Widely used for general shipping cartons.

E flute

Fine and neat

Very thin flute with a smooth surface. Suited to retail boxes and sharp, detailed printing.

Flute types are a general industry guide. Our plant produces A flute 3 ply board, which gives strong cushioning and stacking strength. Whether it suits your product depends on its weight, fragility, stacking height and transport route, so we confirm the board with you before production.

Board strength also depends on the paper quality and weight used for the liners and flute. Heavier products, long-distance transport or tall stacking may need a stronger paper grade or a higher ply construction. 3 ply is an excellent, economical choice for a wide range of light to medium-weight goods.

Corrugated boxes are lightweight, cost-effective and made from paper that can be recycled, which makes them one of the most practical packaging materials for modern businesses.

How to choose the right box.

  • Measure the product: inside length, width and height, in that order
  • Add a small margin for cushioning, not too much, because extra space lets goods move
  • Note the weight of what goes inside, and how high boxes will be stacked
  • Think about the journey: local delivery, long-distance, humid weather
  • Decide how much printing and branding you need

Why packaging matters, and what good packaging does.

Packaging is the first thing a customer touches and the last line of defence for your product. It is not just a box; it is part of your product, your logistics and your brand.

Protects the product

Good packaging absorbs shocks, vibration and stacking pressure during storage and transport, so goods reach the customer undamaged.

Reduces losses

Fewer damaged shipments means fewer returns, replacements and complaints. Strong packaging usually costs far less than the damage it prevents.

Builds your brand

A clean, well-printed box creates a professional first impression and makes your business look dependable and established.

Improves logistics

Right-sized, uniform cartons stack well, fill containers and trucks efficiently, and speed up handling and warehousing.

Communicates clearly

Printed handling marks, labels and product details help everyone in the supply chain treat your goods correctly.

Supports sustainability

Recyclable corrugated board lets you pack responsibly and meet the growing expectations of customers and partners.

Quality and process

How box strength is measured and how an order moves from enquiry to delivery.

What decides how strong a box is.

These are the standard industry measures of corrugated strength. We choose board to suit your product’s weight and stacking needs.

Bursting strength

The pressure the board can take before it bursts. Higher values mean better resistance to rough handling.

Box compression

How much top load a finished box can carry. This tells you how high boxes can safely be stacked.

Edge crush

Resistance of the board edge to crushing. It relates closely to stacking strength.

Paper GSM and BF

Paper weight and bursting factor of the liners and flute. Better paper makes stronger board.

Moisture

Damp board loses strength fast. Dry storage and good paper keep boxes performing.

Flute and ply

Flute height and number of plies set cushioning and load capacity. Ours is 3 ply with A flute.

Storage and handling tips.

  • Store boxes flat, dry and off the floor, ideally on pallets
  • Keep them away from water, leaks and high humidity
  • Do not stack higher than recommended
  • Keep out of long direct sunlight, which fades print
  • Do not overload a box beyond the weight it was chosen for
  • Seal with good tape suited to the weight of the contents

Questions we often hear.

Which flute should I choose?

Our plant makes A flute 3 ply board, which suits products that need good cushioning and stacking strength. Tell us what you pack and we will confirm it is the right fit.

Can you print my logo on the boxes?

Yes. We print in-house. Send your artwork, box size and quantity, and approve the layout before printing.

Do you make custom sizes?

Yes. Boxes can be made to your product dimensions, which reduces movement and damage in transit.

What details do I need for a quote?

Product type, inside box size, weight of contents, quantity, print requirement and delivery location.

How do I measure the box size?

Measure the inside length, width and height, in that order. Length is the longer side of the opening. Allow a small margin for cushioning.

Where do you dispatch from?

From our warehouse in Alipur, New Delhi. Contact us to confirm delivery to your location.

Is corrugated packaging eco-friendly?

Corrugated board is paper-based and widely recycled. Its light weight also helps keep freight costs down.
